sentences: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain’s National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1. 6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients’ rights and their expectations of privacy.
translations: 任何公正评估英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）与DeepMind之间交易风险的人，都必须首先承认双方都是出于善意。DeepMind是全球领先的人工智能公司之一。这项工作应用于医疗保健领域的潜力巨大，但也可能导致科技巨头权力的进一步集中。正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对NHS下属的皇家自由医院信托基金作出了严厉的裁决，该基金在2015年基于一项模糊的协议，将160万患者的记录交给了DeepMind，而这项协议对患者的权利及其隐私期望考虑得太少。

sentences: DeepMind has almost apologised. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements—and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it “controlled” the data and DeepMind merely “processed” it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession
translations: DeepMind 几乎已经道歉了。NHS信托机构也已改正其做法。NHS与DeepMind之间未来的安排——可能还有很多——将受到仔细审查，以确保已向患者征得所有必要许可，并清除所有不必要的数据。在知情患者同意方面，有教训需要吸取。但隐私并非本案的唯一角度，甚至不是最重要的角度。丹纳姆女士选择将责任集中在NHS信托机构上，因为根据现行法律，该机构“控制”数据，而DeepMind仅“处理”数据。但这种区分忽略了一个要点，即关键在于处理和聚合，而非仅仅拥有数据。

sentences: of bits, that gives the data value. The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
translations: 比特的组合，构成了数据值。真正的大问题是，谁应该从我们生活所产生的所有数据分析中获益。隐私法建立在个人因被识别的信息而受到损害的概念之上。这忽略了监控经济的运作方式。在监控经济中，个人的数据只有与数百万人的数据进行比较时，才能获得其价值。

sentences: The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham’s report
translations: 在这种情况下，利用隐私法来约束科技巨头似乎有些不太适用。这种做法并未触及真正的担忧所在。仅说DeepMind开发的算法将惠及患者、挽救生命是不够的。关键在于，这些算法将归属于一家利用公共资源开发它们的私人垄断企业。如果软件能像现在的药物一样大规模地拯救生命，那么大数据或许也会像大型制药公司那样行事。我们仍处于这场革命的初期，现在的小小选择日后可能产生巨大影响。要避免数字封建主义的未来，需要一场长期的斗争。丹纳姆女士的报告

sentences:
31. What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?
A. It fell short of the latter’s expectations.
B. It caused conflicts among tech giants.
C. It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.
D. It put both sides into a dangerous situation.
translations:
31. NHS与DeepMind之间的协议中，哪一项是正确的？
A. 它未达到后者的期望。
B. 它引发了科技巨头之间的冲突。
C. 它未能充分关注患者的权利。
D. 它将双方置于危险的境地。

sentences:
32. The NHS trust responded to Denham’s verdict with
A. empty promises.
B. tough resistance.
C. sincere apologies.
D. necessary adjustments.
translations:

A. 空洞的承诺。
B. 强硬的抵制。
C. 真诚的道歉。
D. 必要的调整。

sentences:
33. The author argues in Paragraph 2 that

B. the value of data comes from the processing of it.
C. making profits from patients’ data is illegal.
D. leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it.

33. 作者在第二段中论证道
A. 隐私保护必须不惜一切代价加以确保。
B. 数据的价值来源于对其的处理。
C. 从患者数据中获利是非法的。
D. 泄露患者数据比出售它更糟糕。

sentences:
34. According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is
A. the monopoly of big data by tech giants.
B. the vicious rivalry among big pharmas.
C. the uncontrolled use of new software.
D. the ineffective enforcement of privacy law.
translations:

A. 科技巨头对大数据的垄断。
B. 大型制药公司之间的恶性竞争。
C. 新软件的不受控制的使用。
D. 隐私法执行不力。
